entries.title: Sean Burke, Davis Martin will need to be durable for White Sox, who lose to Astros
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" >White Sox</a> are going to need <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/07/19/sean-burke-white-sox-toronto-davis-martin-starting-pitchers" target="_blank" >Sean Burke and Davis Martin</a> to be at their best to win the American League Central. That means Burke and Martin will have to breeze past their career highs in innings pitched while staying effective.</p><p>The foundation for them to do that was built last year, when both set their personal marks, albeit when the stakes were much lower.</p><p>On their way to their third straight 100-loss season, the Sox got 142‰ innings from Martin and 134⅓ from Burke. As Martin said, both had “training wheels” on in 2025 because of their respective injury histories: Martin hadn’t pitched a full season since undergoing Tommy John surgery in 2023, and shoulder issues limited Burke in 2023 and 2024.</p><p>“Looking back, it was the best thing for us,” Martin told the Sun-Times on Saturday before the Sox lost to the Astros 4-1. “We had a solid workload last year, so throwing 170-180 innings isn’t going to be too over the top compared to going from 80 innings to 180.”</p><p>That many innings this year is possible for both. The Sox have 59 regular-season games left, and they hope a few more in October.</p><p>Through 20 starts, Martin already has pitched 111 innings. Like Martin did Friday, Burke ran into trouble in the sixth Saturday. After throwing five scoreless innings, Burke loaded the bases with no outs. Isaac Paredes singled to right to bring in two runs, and when Braden Montgomery overran the ball, a third scored.</p><p>The inning was decisive, spoiling an otherwise-solid night for Burke, who was beaten by Hunter Brown’s seven scoreless innings. Burke struck out 10 and didn’t look like a pitcher wearing down at 118⅓ innings.</p><p>“I [am] just taking care of my arm and the on-field results but also trying to stay consistent with my routine in between weeks, too,” Burke said.</p><p>The Sox certainly will monitor him and Martin, but innings limits are not in their future.</p><p>“You just need to be mindful between starts and having an idea of where they’re at, physically, mentally and those things,” manager Will Venable said. “But as far as innings go, that’s not something that’s going to limit us or drive what we do.”</p><p>Knowing that, it’s on the pitchers as much as anybody to stay on their programs to keep themselves on the mound.</p><p>Martin said he has introduced correctives from past back spasms and forearm problems to his regular schedule to try to avoid future issues. He made it past 80 innings healthy, which he couldn’t do last year, when he went on the injured list in June with a forearm strain, interrupting an otherwise durable 2025.</p><p>“The last two to three years have been a really good runway for me to figure out what has and hasn’t worked for me in the past,” Martin said.</p><p>Even if Martin’s methods continue working, it doesn’t mean he’ll feel great the rest of the year. Martin said he spoke with former Sox pitchers Lance Lynn, Martin Perez and Dylan Cease about throwing a lot of innings, and they shared what worked for them.</p><p>“The overview is that no one feels good,” Martin said. “No one feels 100% in October and September. So that is the biggest thing for me mentally, just thinking ‘Hey, you’re going to have to push through some stuff.’ I feel like we’ve already done that this year.”</p><div class="PageListL" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" data-show-loadmore="true" ><a class="AnchorLink" id="list-4a0005" name="list-4a0005"></a><div class="PageList-header" > <div class="PageList-header-title-wrap" > <div class="PageList-header-title"> <a class="" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="{borderColor=#dfdfdf, pageNumber=1, inverseColors=false, footerBgColor=#000000, bodyFont=font-3, items=[{type=Image, timestamp=1785026816000, wordCount=711, _styledTemplate=null, authors=[{authorPageUrl=https://chicago.suntimes.com/barry-m-bloom, name=[{items=[Barry M. entries.title: Motorcyclist dies after crash on DuSable Lake Shore Drive in Lake View
entries.summary: <p>A motorcyclist was killed after crashing Saturday night on DuSable Lake Shore Drive in Lake View.</p><p>The 20-year-old man was driving north in the 2200 block of DuSable Lake Shore Drive around 7:22 p.m. when he lost control and struck a barrier, Chicago police said.</p><p>He fell over the barrier, into oncoming traffic and was struck by a car, police said.</p><p>The man suffered multiple injuries and was taken to Illinois Masonic Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead, police said.</p><p>CPD’s Major Accidents Unit is investigating.</p>

entries.title: WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert keeps her head down, picks her phone up
entries.summary: <p>This just in: WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert plans to text the players more.</p><p>That wasn't Engelbert's only takeaway from All-Star weekend, of course.</p><p>But the plan to "institute more frequent communication," as the former Deloitte CEO put it, stuck out.</p><p>The knock on Engelbert, who is facing mounting public criticism from league insiders, is that her relationship-building needs work. Players feel like they don't hear from her on a regular basis.</p><p>Asked to characterize the current relationship, four-time MVP A'ja Wilson repeated her standard line: She really only knows Engelbert from trophy handoffs.</p><p>Engelbert said she took that feedback this weekend. She's now realizing that players don't really read their emails. She's now realizing they might actually want to hear from her casually, a happy birthday text or check-in after an injury or milestone.</p><p>Is it too little, too late? Maybe. Multiple <a class="Link" href="https://www.espn.com/wnba/story/_/id/49436321/wnba-2026-cathy-engelbert-commissioner-future-all-star-break" target="_blank" >reports</a> from ESPN and Sports Business Journal in recent weeks suggest many league insiders believe this might, or at least should, be her final year.</p><p>One thing most agree on: She has put the league on much more stable financial footing and got a CBA done that made players millionaires. But the office requires savvy in the personal, communication and PR side too.</p><p>Asked whether she plans to be commissioner in 2027, Engelbert gave her usual answer about keeping her head down.</p><p>"I'm so blessed to have to be at the helm of this league during this incredible hyper growth period," she said. "So I will continue to do my job, execute the strategy, because it has been working. Make sure we listen to the players, communicate with the players. Absolutely just love this league."</p><p>For now, she's still chugging away at the priorities: improving officiating, which has remained a pain point this season. Globalizing the game, a standard playbook for professional sports these days. And improving player security, which matters even more in a women's league, where players face disproportionately more threats.</p><p>The last point was the focus of the weekend. League leaders met with players to address the online harassment they increasingly receive. Mercury star Alyssa Thomas recently described death threats after her flagrant foul on Fever star Caitlin Clark. Aces star Chelsea Gray talked about receiving racial slurs from someone who had bet on one of her games.</p><p>Engelbert said the meeting was productive and that the league will invest in enhanced security personnel and protocols.</p><p>On officiating, Engelbert announced an improvement many have called for: Like the NBA, the WNBA will install a replay center for the 2027 season, helping on-court officials make more accurate and efficient decisions when reviewing plays.</p><p>There's still plenty of work to be done for the WNBA's infrastructure to match its quality of play. But the league keeps growing. Engelbert pointed out that 29 games have averaged more than 1 million viewers, up from 11 at this point last year. The All-Star Game set an attendance record with nearly 20,000 fans. </p><p>And the game itself was a delight, with a nice balance of style and comic interludes. Team Spoon, led by MVP Jonquel Jones, won 129-122. The young stars — Caitlin Clark, Olivia Miles, Paige Bueckers and Dominique Malonga — all dazzled.</p><p>As a whole, All-Star weekend painted the picture of a league that's thriving.</p><p>Engelbert is embattled, but she presided over a remarkable transformation: a league once on the margins, now fully mainstream. There's plenty to like about her legacy. If only she'd thought to institute the Texting Initiative a little sooner.</p>

entries.title: MVPETE > Cy Skenes? Pete Crow-Armstrong dazzles as Cubs beat up October-type ace Paul Skenes
entries.summary: <p>PITTSBURGH – <b>Paul Skenes</b> is the type of pitcher the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> are going to have to beat if they’re going to make a deep October run.</p><p>They showed they’re capable of taking it to the game’s best, tagging the Pirates’ ace and reigning NL Cy Young winner for five runs in an 11-0 blowout win Saturday.</p><p>It was another banner night for All-Star center fielder <b>Pete Crow-Armstrong</b>, who won two of his three showdowns with Skenes – his crushed RBI double off the wall started the scoring – and had four hits on the night, homering and coming a triple shy of his second cycle of the season.</p><p>“I love facing Paul,” Crow-Armstrong said of Skenes, a teammate both as a pre-teen and with Team USA in the World Baseball Classic. “He’s one of the best competitors in our sport. I admire that the most about him.</p><p>“I love how he goes about his business. It’s fun to watch that behind the scenes when you get to be in the same clubhouse as him. Taking that personal experience into today with me and into any matchup with him, it’s fun.”</p><p>Skenes is good as big league arms come, once again a candidate for the sport’s top pitching award in a crowded NL field.</p><p>But Crow-Armstrong is having a spectacular season, making the case that he is – as the award states – <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/02/cubs-pete-crow-armstrong-mvp-player-of-the-month-june-stats-babe-ruth-lou-gehrig-shohei-ohtani" >the most valuable player in baseball</a>. He came into Saturday leading the game’s position players with 6.6 fWAR.</p><p>“The best leadoff hitter,” lefty starter <b>Shota Imanaga</b> said through an interpreter. “He can get extra-base hits, he can hit a homer, he can get on, he can steal.</p><p>“If you’re the opposing pitcher and you’re facing him to start a game, that’s tough.”</p><p><b>From Steel City to the North Side</b></p><p>Left fielder <b>Ian Happ</b> walked Saturday, extending his on-base streak in his hometown to a remarkable 43 games, the longest such streak in PNC Park’s history.</p><p>A night earlier, Happ did it all in an extra-inning Cubs win, making big plays with his bat, with his glove and on the base paths.</p><p>“Ian’s amazing,” lefty starter <b>Matthew Boyd</b> said. “It speaks to what he is as a player, what he means to this team.”</p><p>Whether Happ’s 10th season on the North Side is his last – <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/23/seiya-suzuki-walk-up-music-frank-sinatra-my-way-free-agent-contract-home-runs-lineup-payroll" >like outfield-mate <b>Seiya Suzuki</b></a>, Happ’s slated to hit free agency after the season – his experience with the organization has proven valuable inside the Cubs’ clubhouse.</p><p>“He truly embodies what it means to be a Cub,” Boyd said. “He plays the game the right way. You hear his ovation every time he jogs out to left field, from the bleachers. … Some of those things might seem irrelevant to some people, but it is special.</p><p>“He knows the gravity of putting on those pinstripes and what it means to the city and the fans.</p><p>“He’s a direct connection to that 2016 team, too, and he got to play around a lot of champions. Whenever … you get to be around championship players, that stuff wears off on you. He carries himself like a pro, and you can’t put a price tag on that. It’s valuable to all of us.”</p><p><b>Shota shoves</b></p><p>Imanaga threw six shutout innings Saturday. He’s been excellent since a sour four-start stretch earlier this summer, with a 2.00 ERA in his last eight outings, a boon for an injury-plagued Cubs pitching staff.</p><p>“The chances we’ve had when he’s been on the mound this whole year have been plentiful,” Crow-Armstrong said. “He’s pitching exactly like he is capable of, and he’s definitely got some more where that came from, too.”</p>

entries.title: Teresa Weatherspoon, fired by the Sky in 2024, 'absolutely' wants a second crack at coaching in the WNBA
entries.summary: <p>Former <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky" target="_blank" >Sky</a> coach Teresa Weatherspoon didn’t like it when members of the media called her by her first name during press conferences and interviews. “Coach,” “Coach Spoon” or even just “Spoon” was the way she felt it should be. Using her first name was too familiar or not quite reverent enough, seemed to be her position on the matter.</p><p>I didn’t like that she didn’t like it. Or more like I didn’t care. I rolled my eyes so hard at it, they might still be rolling.</p><p>But you know what? I can be a real ninny. As I learned just this weekend — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky-and-wnba/2024/09/26/sky-fire-coach-teresa-weatherspoon-after-one-season" target="_blank" >nearly two years after the Sky fired her</a> — Weatherspoon’s objection wasn’t about ego or hubris. It was nothing more than where she comes from and how she was raised.</p><p>I picked this up watching her seven-month-old appearance on former Sky star Angel Reese’s podcast, “pologetically Angel.” In it, Weatherspoon described her childhood in rural east Texas, in a tiny town where the two most oft-spoken words were “sir” and “ma’am.” All adults were addressed that way, according to Weatherspoon, who is 60. It wasn’t an expectation but rather a demand.</p><p>Maybe I’d have figured this out sooner had she been here for longer than one season before the Sky showed her the door. One year isn’t much time to get to know anybody in any setting, especially if you’re a know-it-all columnist showing up around a team only every now and then.</p><p>Weatherspoon was at the United Center Saturday in the capacity of “general manager” of one of the WNBA All-Star teams — a nod to her excellence as one of the 30-year-old league’s first star players — so I asked her about it. No, not about the name thing. About the kicked-to-the-curb-after-only-one-year thing.</p><p>“Nothing stops the show,” she said twice. “I’m not the only person in the world that this has happened to, you know? I’m not.</p><p>“But one thing about me, it doesn’t hold me down. Nothing holds me down and I move forward, and that’s the most important thing is moving forward and knowing who you are and what you bring. … No one can stop that.”</p><p>Weatherspoon has a job coaching in the Unrivaled league, but she would “absolutely” like to get another crack at the WNBA.</p><p>She won a national championship as a point guard at Louisiana Tech, where she later took the reins as coach. She was the WNBA’s first assists and steals champion as a rookie and became a five-time All-Star. Before going to the Sky, she was an NBA assistant coach with the Pelicans. But when it comes to being a WNBA head coach, all she has on her résumé is a one-and-done with the Sky in 2024.</p><p>Talk about a kick in the gut. It had to hurt.</p><p>“It was a tremendous shock for me,” Weatherspoon said on Reese’s podcast.</p><p>The stuff of coaching and leading has coursed through Weatherspoon’s veins since she first picked up a ball, she recalls.</p><p>“I love it,” she said. “I love just studying it. I love the grit and grind of it all, and then the wit — like how quickly [things] have to happen — and the challenge of it all, and then playing chess. entries.title: It took awhile, but Andruw Jones, Carlos Beltran, Jeff Kent made Baseball Hall of Fame
entries.summary: <p>COOPERSTOWN, N.Y. — If there’s a theme that runs through the induction ceremony Sunday for the National Baseball Hall of Fame on the stage behind the Clark Sports Center, it’s that the three players had to wait.</p><p>There’s no Derek Jeter, Ichiro Suzuki or Mariano Rivera, who all played for one team. No first-time ballot inductees in this group.</p><p>It still will be a singular moment, one Carlos Beltran wondered if he’d ever experience. He made it on his third try in January, receiving votes on 84.2% of the 425 ballots filed by eligible members of the Baseball Writers’ Association of America. Andruw Jones, in his ninth try, earned 78.4% of the vote. The baseline is 75%. Jeff Kent was elected last year by the 16-member Contemporary Baseball Era Committee after 10 years when the BBWAA passed.</p><p>“I appreciate all the reporters that voted for me,” Beltran said. “And for those who didn’t vote for me, I also respect their perspective, how they made their judgment. That being said, I’m going to enjoy this moment.”</p><p>Beltran was entangled in the Astros’ sign-stealing scandal of 2017. The Astros defeated the Dodgers in a seven-game World Series that is forever tainted. The active players were given immunity during the MLB investigation that followed. The coaches, manager and executive were not.</p><p>He was no longer active. On Nov. 19, 2019, he was named manager of the Mets. Then he lost that chance. When MLB issued its scathing report on Jan. 13, 2020, Beltran was the only player named. He was retired and had fallen between the cracks.</p><p>Beltran, who played 20 seasons from 1998 to 2017 for seven teams, including the Yankees and Mets, wondered if he’d ever get into the Hall.</p><p>“It was a possibility,” Beltran said. “You know what? Everything is a possibility in life. I have to say when the Astros situation happened, at the beginning, the first couple of years, there were people who didn’t vote for me, but they voted for me after three years. The question will be: What changed for them? What changed their mind to reward me to get elected to the Hall of Fame?”</p><p>Times change. People are sometimes forgiven for their transgressions.</p><p>Jones played 17 seasons with five teams, but he was best known for his first 12 as a 10-time Gold Glove-winning center fielder for the Braves. During his last five seasons, he gained weight and nearly fell off the map playing for four teams — the Dodgers, Rangers, White Sox and Yankees. He finished his career in Japan. Jones was a .254 lifetime hitter with 434 homers. In those last five big-league seasons, he hit .210 with only 66 homers.</p><p>Near the end of his 10-year tenure on the BBWAA ballot, the writers had a change of heart.</p><p>Jones is now one of six players from those 1990s Braves to make the Hall of Fame, including Tom Glavine, Greg Maddux, John Smoltz, Chipper Jones and Fred McGriff. Late manager Bobby Cox and general manager John Schuerholz also are in the Hall. All of Jones’ former teammates are here for the ceremony.</p><p>“We all sat down at a round table [Friday],” Jones said. “They called to congratulate me. They kept saying, ‘Be patient. You’re going to be there.’ It was a battle for nine years. You try not to think about it because life keeps going.”</p><p>Kent played 17 years for six teams and despite having the most homers for a second baseman — 351 of his 377 homers playing that position — never earned any traction on the BBWAA ballot. He peaked at 46.5% in his 10th and final season. But last year, a 16-member era committee picked him as the only electee from the eight players on the ballot. He needed 12 votes. Kent said Saturday he felt like a “cool cat” a day before making his speech.</p><p>“I can handle it, so right now I’m good,” he said. But Sunday?</p><p>“I’m going to have anxiety at the level that I’m going to need some drugs to calm me down,” he added.</p><p>For these guys, it has been that kind of roller-coaster experience for years.</p><p><b>2026 BASEBALL HALL OF FAME INDUCTEES</b></p><p><b>• Carlos Beltran</b>, center fielder<br><b>• Andruw Jones</b>,<b> </b>center fielder<br><b>• Jeff Kent</b>,<b> </b>second baseman<br><b>• Joe Buck</b>,<b> </b>Ford C. entries.title: Fire drop second straight since returning from break
entries.summary: <p>NEW YORK — Nicolas Fernandez scored a goal for the third consecutive game, Agustin Ojeda and Malachi Jones each added a goal and New York City FC beat the Fire 3-1 on Saturday night.</p><p>Joel Waterman scored his first goal this season for the Fire (8-6-2), who have lost back-to-back games after a three-game winning streak before going on the World Cup break. Both losses have come since the addition of Polish star Robert Lewandowski.</p><p>Ojeda, on the counter-attack, ran onto a through ball played ahead by Andrés Perea and bent a shot from the right side of the area off the back post and into the net to make it 2-1 in the 29th.</p><p>Fernandez blasted a first-touch shot, off a clearance played by Jack Elliott, from 25 yards out to open the scoring in the 10th minute.</p><p>Waterman tied it at 1-all in the 21st minute. Anton Saletros played a free kick from the right sideline that was redirected by Ojeda’s header at the front post, and Waterman tapped it inside the back post from point-blank range.</p><p>Jones' first goal since 2024 gave NYCFC a two-goal lead in the 41st minute. Perea played a ball ahead to Ojeda, who tapped a cross from the right side of the area to Jones for a first-touch finish from point-blank range.</p><p>Matt Freese had FOUR saves for NYCFC (7-6-4).<br></p>

entries.title: Brother Rice DL Brayden Parks is third top-10 player from Illinois headed to Irish in 2027 recruiting cycle
entries.summary: <p>Notre Dame football’s recruiting push in Chicago continues to pay big dividends.</p><p>On Thursday, Brother Rice defensive lineman Brayden Parks announced his commitment to the Fighting Irish on CBS Sports College Football’s YouTube channel.</p><p>Parks, whose godfather is former Vocational and Notre Dame star Chris Zorich, is the third top-10 player from Illinois landed by Irish coach Marcus Freeman in the 2027 recruiting cycle.</p><p>All are from the Catholic League — St. Patrick defensive lineman David Folrunsho and Mount Carmel linebacker Roman Igwebuike are the others — and all are consensus top-200 players nationally. Parks is the No. 10 player in Illinois, the No. 24 defensive lineman and the No. 199 player nationally in the 247Sports composite rankings.</p><p>The Irish have been stocking up on local defensive linemen in recent years. Already on the roster are Simeon’s Christopher Burgess Jr., IC Catholic’s Dominik Hulak and York’s Joe Reiff.</p><p>Parks, a 6-3, 305-pounder, had more than 40 offers and cut his list of potential destinations to Notre Dame and Oregon.</p><p>He talked about his recruiting on the YouTube video: “It’s a long time coming, but at the end of the day, it’s a blessing.”</p><p>His wish list?</p><p>“I was looking for a team that’s going to be in the playoffs every year, a team that has a chance of winning a national championship.”</p><p>He also was looking for a strong connection with his coaches, who will include Freeman, defensive line coach Charlie Partridge and assistant defensive line coach Nick Sebastian.</p><p>“Just talking to coach Freeman, it shows he cares [about me], not just as a football player but as a person,” Parks said. “I’ve known coach Sebastian since I started my recruiting process about four years ago and then coach [Partridge] came into it this January.”</p><p>Parks is coming off a productive season for the Class 7A champion Crusaders. He had 61 tackles, 7œ sacks, 23 tackles for loss and an interception en route to being named Defensive Player of the Year in the rugged CCL/ESCC Blue.</p><p>National recruiting analyst Clint Cosgrove sees a bright future for Parks at Notre Dame.</p><p>“The kid is an absolute beast,” Cosgrove said. “The size/frame combination is very rare. It’s hard to find those big defensive tackles who can push those double-teams back and also rush the passer.</p><p>“He’s the complete package.”</p><p>And as good as Parks is now, Cosgrove said, “he’s just going to get bigger, better, stronger. . . . His best football is in front of him.”</p><h3>More on 2027 prospects</h3><p>With Parks picking Notre Dame, the vast majority of the state’s top prospects will be committed when high school practice starts Aug. 5. That doesn’t mean there won’t be any more recruiting news coming, though. In every cycle, some recruits flip schools, decommitting from one and picking another.</p><p>And there are still a few high-level prospects who haven’t made a decision. The state’s top-ranked uncommitted player in the rising senior class is No. 23 Lawrence Carr, a receiver from Kenwood.</p><p>The early signing period for football will be Dec. 4-6, with the traditional signing day scheduled for Feb. 5, 2027.<br></p>
